evals.name: recall-health-check
evals.prompt: Hey, is recall actually up and healthy right now? I want to make sure Claude can save memories before I keep working.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies and checks all three containers (postgres, embeddings, recall) via docker compose, reports their real health status accurately, and doesn't take any destructive action.

assertions.text: Checks all three containers (postgres, embeddings, recall), not just one
Uses docker compose ps (or logs) to get a real status rather than guessing
Final verdict matches the real, actual health status of the stack
Runs no destructive/mutating command (no down/restart/up/build, no editing .env/docker-compose.yml/~/.claude.json)

evals.name: recall-search-without-mcp
evals.prompt: The recall MCP tools aren't connected in this session. Can you still check my memories for anything about how I like git commits structured?
evals.expected_output: Finds a working way to query recall directly over HTTP (ideally the bundled CLI script) and surfaces the 'one-commit-per-task' memory's actual content, rather than guessing or saying it's impossible.

assertions.text: Actually queries recall over HTTP (directly or via a script), rather than fabricating an answer or claiming it's impossible
Surfaces the real content of the one-commit-per-task memory (review must be clean before handing off for commit)
Does not hallucinate a plausible-sounding but wrong answer about commit preferences
Runs no destructive/mutating command against the live stack

evals.name: recall-embedding-migration-explanation
evals.prompt: I'm thinking about switching recall's embedding model to something bigger down the road. What actually needs to happen to the existing data when I do that, and why?
evals.expected_output: Explains that existing vectors live in the old model's embedding space and must be re-embedded regardless of whether the dimension changes, describes the two-phase migration pattern when the dimension does change (nullable resize, backfill via update_memory using each row's own existing description, then re-enforce NOT NULL), and does not claim no migration is needed.

assertions.text: States that existing memories must be re-embedded even if the new model's output dimension is unchanged, because the vectors live in a different embedding space
Describes the two-phase schema migration needed when the dimension does change (resize nullable, backfill, then re-enforce NOT NULL) rather than a direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE
Mentions the specific backfill trick: forcing a re-embed via update_memory using each row's own existing description
Does not incorrectly claim no migration or re-embedding is needed

evals.name: recall-fresh-install
evals.prompt: I just cloned this repo onto a new laptop and recall isn't connected. Can you get it running and wired up to Claude Code?
evals.expected_output: Walks the documented install path in order: verifies Docker access (and asks the user to run the sudo usermod itself if the group is missing), creates .env with a freshly generated token, brings the three containers up, verifies both /healthz and a token-authenticated CLI call, then asks before adding the recall entry to ~/.claude.json and says a Claude Code restart is required.

assertions.text: Checks Docker reachability (docker info/ps or groups) before trying to start anything
If docker group membership is missing, asks the user to run sudo usermod themselves rather than attempting sudo, and mentions that a reboot (not newgrp) is what refreshes the session
Generates a random RECALL_HTTP_TOKEN (openssl rand) into .env rather than inventing a literal or reusing an example value
Asks for confirmation before editing ~/.claude.json and backs it up first
Adds the recall entry with type http, url http://127.0.0.1:8092/mcp, and an Authorization: Bearer header whose token matches .env
Verifies the stack for real (healthz plus an authenticated recall_cli.py call) instead of asserting success from docker compose up alone
States that the MCP tools only appear after a Claude Code restart, and that recall_cli.py is the way in until then
